input: This passage reports the results of batch adsorption tests in which the adsorption of a dye from water on a metal-organic framework was measured at 298 K. The experimental data were fitted using the Langmuir model, and the fitted Langmuir capacity was 235 mg of dye per gram of adsorbent at pH 5. In a further test carried out at an adsorbent dose of 0.6 g L-1, removal after 120 min was 83% of the initial dye concentration of 50 mg L-1. These results provide a useful indication of the capacity of the material and of the level of removal achieved under the particular conditions examined. However, it is important to note that the Langmuir fit is reported for pH 5 only, and capacity at other pH values was not measured. As a result, the reported capacity should be understood in the context of the conditions under which it was obtained, and it should not be assumed that the same capacity applies across a broader range of pH conditions than those actually investigated in the batch tests. The findings should consequently be read as a linked set of results that apply to the conditions of the tests themselves. The fitted capacity describes the adsorbent through the Langmuir representation, the removal result describes what was achieved at the stated dose over the stated contact period, and the pH limitation defines the boundary within which the capacity figure has actually been established by measurement.
target: Adsorption of a dye from water on a metal-organic framework was measured in batch tests at 298 K. The fitted Langmuir capacity was 235 mg of dye per gram of adsorbent at pH 5. At an adsorbent dose of 0.6 g L-1, removal after 120 min was 83% of the initial dye concentration of 50 mg L-1. The capacity and the removal figure describe different aspects of the same tests. The Langmuir capacity is the fitted saturation capacity of the adsorbent under the model. The removal value is the fraction of the initial dye taken up at the stated dose and contact time. Neither figure extends the pH range of the work. The Langmuir fit is reported for pH 5 only; capacity at other pH values was not measured. The results therefore hold at that pH, at the stated temperature, dose and contact time, and the capacity should not be carried to other pH values as if it had been measured there. Read together, the figures give a bounded picture of the material. The capacity comes from a model fit and carries the model's form with it. The removal figure comes from a direct batch outcome at the stated dose and time. The pH statement then prevents the most likely misreading of the pair of results, which would be to treat a capacity fitted at one pH as a property of the adsorbent at every pH. The passage keeps the property where the measurement put it.
